title: Phases of the forcing law, and what overlap does to them
claim: On atom patterns with held distinctions, a distinction's phase under the forcing law (two-place reasoning per phase) equals the least Strahler number of its derivation trees (known: Esparza-Kiefer-Luttenberger); the phase count is at most log2 of the fringe (known, Ullman-Van Gelder) and at most log2 |H| without reuse (known-with-delta); more phases than log2 |H| need a rejoining; the wall (P-completeness, Goldschlager, Cook's path systems) needs both reuse and several-way demand unless P = NC or P = NL; of the 34 three-place knot laws 2 are AC0, 2 parity-L-complete, 14 P-complete and 16 NP-complete (known, Schaefer, Allender et al., applied); not-all-equal propagation is P-complete with two held values; on acyclic patterns a dual law spreading unforcedness decides the forced set in O(min(P, P_dual) log^2 n) parallel time.
standard_statement: Horn least-model computation by Newton iterates (Boolean semiring): iterate count = least Horton-Strahler number of derivation trees; NC for polylogarithmic Strahler number; polynomial fringe; monotone formulas; AND-only circuits in NL; MCVP P-complete; Boolean CSP classification with constants for the 34 three-ary relations that are free on every pair and not full; NAE unit propagation P-complete; dual Newton iteration for the greatest fixed point on acyclic systems.
prior_work: Esparza, Kiefer and Luttenberger 2010; Esparza, Luttenberger and Schlund 2014; Ullman and Van Gelder 1988; Ruzzo 1980; Buss 1987; Miller and Reif 1985; Goldschlager 1977; Cook 1974; Jones and Laaser 1976; Schaefer 1978; Allender, Bauland, Immerman, Schnoor and Vollmer 2009; Baker and Pixley 1975; Kasif 1990; Berman, Idziak, Markovic, McKenzie, Valeriote and Willard 2010.
